summary:
[  edit  ]
The Delete  CHOP  removes entire channels and/or individual samples of its input.
For deleting channels, on the Channels page, you can specify which channels to delete by channel name or a channel number range. A second method deletes channels using a value range to select channels whose values are all within a range. The third method deletes constant-valued channels. An option selects whether to delete or retain the matched channels.
For deleting individual samples (i.e. no channels are deleted), on the Samples page you can delete, for example, only the samples whose value is below 0, which will shorten the length of the  CHOP .
In CHOPs with two or more channels, one or more "compare" channels are used to determine which samples are to be deleted. By default it uses the first channel to compare against. Deleting a sample at a certain index deletes a value for all the channels. If there are 4 channels,  red ,  green ,  blue ,  alpha  and you specify  alpha  as the "compare" channel, you can delete all the samples with an  alpha  of  0 . If a  CHOP  is 3 channels with an X,Y,Z position, you can delete all samples where the XYZ length is below a threshold.
This is useful, for example, for thinning your data before sending a  CHOP  to a Geometry component for instancing.

parameters.label: Delete Channels
parameters.name: delchannels
parameters.description: Toggle to enable channel deleting.

parameters.label: Delete
parameters.name: discard
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines whether the scoped channels should be deleted or retained:

parameters.label: Scoped Channels
parameters.name: scoped

parameters.label: Non-scoped Channels
parameters.name: nonscoped
parameters.description: The scoped channels are output. The rest are deleted.

parameters.label: Select Channels
parameters.name: select
parameters.description: ⊞  - How to select channels -  By Name , or By  Numeric  index.

parameters.label: Channel Names
parameters.name: delscope
parameters.description: Enter a scope pattern here to specify the names of channels to delete or extract. You do this by specifying a scope pattern, as detailed in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Channel Numbers
parameters.name: selnumbers
parameters.description: The indices of the channels to delete or extract. - See possible number patterns below.

parameters.label: Channel Value
parameters.name: chanvalue
parameters.description: ⊞  - Chooses the type of value range selection:

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't perform range selection.

parameters.label: Channel Completely Within Range
parameters.name: complete
parameters.description: All the channel's samples must be within the specified range for it to be selected.

parameters.label: Channel Partially Within Range
parameters.name: partial
parameters.description: At least one of the channel's samples must be in the range for it to be selected.

parameters.label: Channel Completely Outside Range
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: None of the channel's samples can be in the range for it to be selected.

parameters.label: Value Range
parameters.name: selrange
parameters.description: ⊞  - The lower and upper values of the range used for Range Selection.

parameters.label: Select Constant Valued Channels
parameters.name: selconst
parameters.description: Select channels which have the same value for all samples. These kinds of channel name patterns are used to select existing channels in an input  CHOP , see  Pattern Matching  for details.
Matches the first, second and fifth channel.

parameters.label: Delete Samples
parameters.name: delsamples
parameters.description: Toggle to enable sample deleting.

parameters.label: Channels to Compare
parameters.name: compchans
parameters.description: ⊞  - How to select channels used to compare against criteria - By  Name , by  Numeric  index, by using the  First  Channel  , or by using the  Last  Channel  .

parameters.label: Channel Names
parameters.name: compnames
parameters.description: Enter a scope pattern here to specify the names of channels to be used as compare channels. You do this by specifying a scope pattern, as detailed in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Channel Numbers
parameters.name: compnums
parameters.description: The indices of the channels to be used as compare channels, the default being  0 , the first channel. - See possible number patterns above.

parameters.label: Multi-Compare Channels
parameters.name: compmulti
parameters.description: ⊞  - If there is more that one compare channel, this determines how to treat the values in the compare channels before checking against the criteria:

parameters.label: Any Chan in Range
parameters.name: any
parameters.description: Delete the sample if any of the compare channels meets the criteria.

parameters.label: All Chans in Range
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Delete the sample if all the compare channels meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Add
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Add all the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.name: sub
parameters.description: Subtract all the compare channels from the first and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Multiply
parameters.name: mul
parameters.description: Multiply all the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Divide
parameters.name: div
parameters.description: Divide the first channel by rest of the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Average
parameters.name: avg
parameters.description: Find the average of all the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Find the minimum of all the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Find the maximum of all the compare channels and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Assume all the compare channels are vectors and find their length, and delete the sample if the result meets the criteria.

parameters.label: Delete Condition
parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose the criteria for the samples to be compare against:

parameters.description: Delete if the comparing samples are equal to Value 1.

parameters.label: Not Equal to Value 1
parameters.name: notequal
parameters.description: Delete if the comparing samples are not equal to Value 1.

parameters.label: Inside Range
parameters.name: inside
parameters.description: Delete if the comparing samples are inside the range assigned by Value 1 and Value 2.

parameters.label: Outside Range
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Delete if the comparing samples are outside the range assigned by Value 1 and Value 2.

parameters.label: Value 1
